<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This tracker keeps the dense Qwen3-8B TPU inference parity matrix readable and current for Levanter versus vLLM-TPU. The matrix is meant to report separate regime rows instead of a single average, covering decode-heavy, mixed, prefill-heavy, pressure, churn, sampled `n=4`, greedy `n=1`, and longer output cases with throughput, token-completion, admission, and timing fields. Current anchors show Levanter close on v6e decode-heavy (`0.938` decode tok/s ratio), below target on v6e mixed (`0.819`), still below target on v6e prefill-heavy after corrected and post-split reruns (`0.742` to `0.758`), and substantially behind on the bounded v5p TP=4 mixed row (`0.600`). The current recommendation is to avoid automatic matrix reruns from this tracker: after PR #6185 lands or maintainers explicitly authorize reruns from that head, refresh the highest-value v6e decode-heavy and corrected mixed rows first; do not spend more runs on the prefill-heavy row unless #6229 chooses another optimization experiment, and treat v5p follow-up as a throughput-gap investigation tracked by #6230.

### Helpful links
- Parent rollout epic: #6227
- Dense matrix harness PR: #6176
- Admission/timing fields PR: #6185
- Prefill-heavy follow-up: #6229
- v5p follow-up: #6230
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Finish and maintain the dense Qwen3-8B TPU inference parity matrix for Levanter versus vLLM-TPU. Report results by regime instead of collapsing them into one average: greedy `n=1`, sampled `n=4`, `o128`, `o512`, likely `o2048`, logprobs on/off, decode-heavy, mixed, prefill-heavy, pressure, and churn cases.

PR #6176 (`codex/qwen3-dense-parity-matrix`, head `104bf901e33c5f0b34d32d4f59edf27b82f66714`) carries the dense matrix harness/config and has all visible checks green. PR #6185 head `f55913d1a9770b7ebdfb051150972e649644526e` adds the current admission/timing fields needed for the next rows, including the prefill-drain versus generation-loop split.

Current runtime anchors:
- v6e decode-heavy `decode_b32_i1_o128_n4`: `3197.58` Levanter vs `3408.09` vLLM decode tok/s, ratio `0.938`.
- v6e mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`: `4084.24` Levanter vs `4985.21` vLLM decode tok/s, ratio `0.819`, all `16384` expected completion tokens.
- v6e prefill-heavy `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1`: initial ratio `0.797`, corrected backend=both rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillcorr-20260607-0023` remained an end-to-end target failure at `0.742`, and post-split rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillpostsplit-20260607-0419` remains a target failure at `0.758`. The post-split row shows `1614.816` generation tok/s and only `0.171s` prefill drain in the measured iteration; the remaining decision is tracked in #6229.
- v5p mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`: TP=8 startup retry failed because vLLM/tpu_inference saw only 4 devices; bounded TP=4 retry `/dlwh/qwen3-mixed-v5p-startupdiag-tp4-i512-o512-20260607-0724` succeeded but is a target failure at `0.600` (`3131.59` Levanter vs `5215.67` vLLM decode tok/s; `6263.19` vs `10431.34` total tok/s), with all `16384` completion tokens produced.

### Definition of Done
- [x] Matrix rows are reproducible from committed benchmark config.
- [x] Each row records backend, shape, throughput, token completion, admission/chunking metrics, and pass/fail target in the harness output.
- [ ] v6e-8 rows cover the core RL rollout regimes with current #6185 timing/admission metrics.
- [ ] v5p rows are produced after the v5p startup issue is understood or bypassed.
- [x] Current anchors are linked from the RL rollout epic and handoff PR.

### Current Next Step
Do not launch matrix runs automatically from this tracker. Once #6185 `f55913d1`/`d63d1edf` lands, or maintainers explicitly authorize reruns from that head, refresh the highest-value v6e rows first: the canonical decode-heavy RL row and the corrected mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1` row. Skip additional prefill-heavy `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1` rows unless #6229 explicitly chooses another optimization experiment. Use the new `generation_*` and `prefill_drain_*` fields when interpreting prefill-heavy rows; the collected post-split row shows the generation loop is not the weak point. For v5p, use TP=4 on `v5p-8`; #6230 now has a real mixed row and the remaining question is the `0.600` throughput gap, not startup evidence.

### Parent
- #6227

Current proof points: PR #6176 carries the dense Qwen3 matrix harness and is green; PR #6185 proves the v6e mixed long-prompt correctness fix, the `0.819` vLLM ratio for `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`, bounded request logging, vLLM startup log tails, the `f55913d1` prefill-drain/generation timing split, the post-split #6229 row showing `0.758` end-to-end but `1614.816` generation tok/s for `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1`, and the `d63d1edf` move of the v6e diagnostic log into `.agents/ops/`; it is terminal green/skipped after one external HF/cache rerun; PR #6214 is the durable handoff, is non-draft/ready for review, and is terminal green/skipped at docs-only head `ebbe9a69d` after clarifying review/landing order and correcting the checked-in current-state head; previous heads `67e9500fc`, `2c43f0d91`, and `dbc3bf595` were also terminal green/skipped; PR #6186 carries the token-native rollout API/data-plane slice and is green; PR #6240 is the ready-for-review v5p startup diagnostics hardening, rebased onto #6185 `d63d1edf`, and is terminal green/skipped after the post-rebase checks, including `levanter-tpu-tests`; the bounded v5p TP=4 retry now proves vLLM can start on `v5p-8` when TP matches the 4 visible devices, but the mixed row is a target failure at `0.600` Levanter/vLLM.

- Canonical decode-heavy v6e RL rollout row remains at least `0.90` of vLLM-TPU.
- Mixed long-prompt workloads complete all expected tokens or fail loudly.
- Dense Qwen3-8B matrix is reported by regime with pass/fail status.

issues.title: [Epic] Levanter TPU RL rollout backend parity

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
🤖 Filed by an agent (`agent-generated`) as a follow-up to the overlay-accessor fix for the split-slice bugs (#2/#3 in the control-plane audit).

## Context

Within a single reconcile batch, the apply pass applies per-`(task, attempt)` updates sequentially against a shared `WorkingState` overlay. Guards that read **raw snapshot** state (instead of the overlay) make the outcome depend on the non-deterministic order workers are processed (`worker_provider` async gather). The immediate split-slice instances are being fixed by adding the missing overlay-aware `WorkingState.attempt_state()` accessor and pointing the ~6 reconcile guards at it (twin of the existing `task_state()` accessor).

That targeted fix removes order-dependence for attempt/task **state** reads (the complete set today), but it relies on **per-guard discipline**: any new guard that reads a raw snapshot field can reintroduce order-dependence. Non-state row fields are already read raw — `failure_count`, `max_retries_failure`, `current_attempt_id` — which a same-batch `TaskRowDelta` could in principle make stale.

## Proposal

Make order-independence **structural** rather than per-guard. Two candidate approaches:

1. **Per-task update coalescing** — collect all updates targeting a given `(task, attempt)` within a batch and resolve them by priority (terminal > requeue > running-repoll) before applying once, so arrival order cannot matter.
2. **Overlay-only invariant** — enforce "no reconcile guard dereferences raw `snapshot.attempts`/`snapshot.tasks` state once an overlay exists" via a lint/assertion, so the per-guard discipline is mechanically guaranteed.

## Acceptance

A property/permutation test that shuffles worker-processing order within a batch and asserts identical final DB state (`deterministic_dump`) across all permutations — the durable regression guard the per-instance fixes don't provide.

This issue is a **follow-up to that PR** and is effectively blocked behind it until it lands.

On that branch, the apply pass already uses `state.task_state()` for the in-batch state guards in [`batches.py` `apply_reconcile_batch`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L283) and [`apply_terminal_decisions_batch`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L465). The remaining raw reads are the per-update kernel in [`task.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L349) which still pulls `task.failure_count`, `task.preemption_count`, `task.current_attempt_id`, `task.max_retries_failure`/`_preemption` straight off `snapshot.tasks` (lines 349, 392, 445–446, 492, 497). Same for `snapshot.attempts` at line 350 → `attempt.state`, `attempt.finished_at_ms`, `attempt.worker_id` (lines 381, 415–422, 439). Each of these can in principle be made stale within a batch by an earlier `TaskRowDelta`/`AttemptRowDelta`.

Order source: `reconcile_workers_async` gathers worker plans concurrently, so the per-worker arrival order in `plan_results` (the iteration order of the apply loop) is non-deterministic.

**Relevant code (branch `weaver/iris-reconcile-performance`)**
- [`task.py#L349-L350`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L349-L350) — raw `snapshot.tasks` / `snapshot.attempts` dereference at top of per-update kernel
- [`task.py#L445-L497`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L445-L497) — `failure_count`, `preemption_count`, `max_retries_*` read raw and used for retry-vs-terminal branching
- [`working_state.py#L127-L132`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/working_state.py#L127-L132) — `task_state()` accessor; no `attempt_state` / `task_row` / `attempt_row` counterpart yet
- [`batches.py#L283`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L283) — `apply_reconcile_batch` loop; per-worker iteration order is the order-dependence source

# Analysis of the two proposals

**Approach 1 (per-(task, attempt) coalescing).** As stated this would coalesce duplicate observations for the same `(task, attempt)`. That collision is rare — within one batch each worker emits one observation per attempt, so the realistic order-dependence is **across attempts of the same task or across the task vs its peer-cascade** (`failure_count` accumulation, `current_attempt_id` rotation, sibling requeue races). Coalescing at `(task, attempt)` granularity would not catch the cross-attempt case; coalescing at task granularity would, but loses per-attempt fidelity for the kernel's stale-attempt branch (`update.attempt_id != task.current_attempt_id`). Also: the kernel has side-effects (`record_worker_build_failed`, peer cascade fan-out, recompute work-list) that would need to be split out or proven associative under coalescing. High blast radius.

**Approach 2 (overlay-only invariant).** Add the missing accessors — `WorkingState.task_row(task_id) -> ActiveTaskRow | None` and `WorkingState.attempt_row(task_id, attempt_id) -> AttemptRow | None` — each layering the delta accumulator over the snapshot. Repoint the four raw reads in `task.py` (and the `_apply_single_update` attempt fetch) at the overlay. Then add an AST purity check alongside the existing [`test_reconcile_path_purity.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/tests/cluster/controller/test_reconcile_path_purity.py) that forbids `snapshot.tasks[...]` / `snapshot.attempts[...]` / `.<field>` traversal inside the apply path. Surgical, builds directly on the PR #5987 substrate. Cost is per-field overlay fold extension (`TaskRowDelta` already carries `failure_count`/`preemption_count`; `AttemptRowDelta` already carries `state`/`finished_at`/`error`).

**Recommendation: Approach 2.** Smaller, additive, leans on the AST guard precedent PR #5987 already establishes. The `(task, attempt)` coalescer in Approach 1 is the wrong scope for the actual race, and refactoring the kernel's side-effects to be coalescing-safe is a much larger change than wiring two accessors and a lint.

The **permutation property test** in the Acceptance criterion is approach-independent and should land alongside whichever fix is chosen: shuffle the iteration order of `plan_results` in `apply_reconcile_batch`, materialize via `deterministic_dump`, assert all permutations are equal. The replay-golden harness in [`tests/cluster/controller/replay/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/tests/cluster/controller/replay) is the natural host.

# Sequencing

1. Wait for PR #5987 to merge (`WorkingState`, `ControllerEffects`, AST purity guard).
2. Add `task_row()` / `attempt_row()` overlay accessors on `WorkingState`.
3. Repoint `task._apply_single_update` raw dereferences.
4. Extend the AST purity guard with `snapshot.tasks`/`snapshot.attempts` ban inside `apply_*_batch`.
5. Land the permutation test.

Stopping here — choosing Approach 1 vs 2 and the test's host file are decisions for the PR #5987 author. Not opening a PR until that lands.

## Summary

This sweep investigated recurrent NaNs in `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp` by running a region-pinned v6e-4 learning-rate sweep and then a larger v6e-32 confirmation. The useful result was that the default-style `lr=3e-3, warmup=1000` run stayed finite through 400 steps and beat the `2e-3` run on loss; a v6e-32 confirmation reached step 500 successfully. Further sweep breadth was blocked by repeated Iris launch kills, so the practical conclusion is that the parallel-attn-mlp path had a reproducible non-NaN setting, with infra instability limiting broader hyperparameter exploration.

### Helpful links
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/3316#issuecomment-4010637025
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/3316#issuecomment-4014263360
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Parallel-attn-mlp Grug runs on Nemotron mix have shown recurrent `NaN` loss behavior. We need a controlled hyperparameter sweep on `v6e-4` to find stable (non-NaN) settings before scaling back up.

## Hypothesis or Goal
Find at least one reproducible hyperparameter configuration for `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp` that does not enter NaN over an initial stability window.

Success metrics:
- primary: no `NaN` in `train/loss` through at least 400 steps
- secondary: finite eval losses at first eval checkpoint
- tertiary: stable gradient norms (no `NaN` in `grad/norm/total` watch intervals)

Initial hypotheses:
- effective LR schedule is too aggressive for the parallel residual variant
- longer warmup and/or lower peak LR should prevent early numerical failure
- stronger stabilizers (`z_loss_weight`, lower `max_grad_norm`) may help if LR-only tuning is insufficient

- LR sweep (holding other vars fixed): `3e-3`, `2e-3`, `1e-3`, `5e-4`
- then warmup sweep around best LR: `1000`, `2000`, `4000`
- then stabilization sweep if needed: `z_loss_weight` and `max_grad_norm`

Fixed baseline case:
- `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp/launch.py` default optimizer/trainer settings
- run on `v6e-4` so hardware stays constant during the sweep

Stop criteria:
- stop when we get at least one `replicated` non-NaN config (>=2 runs) or when all planned one-axis sweeps fail and we need architecture-level changes.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Aborting a table-spec migration reverts the table to the legacy path but leaves the objects the migration already wrote under `_finelog/tables/<table>/` with no sweeper: `collect_objects` in `store/table/maintenance.rs` returns early when the table is not object-backed, so the aborted table's own GC loop never runs again.

Observed on marin-dev during the #8748 staging validation: aborting `iris.provisioning` at 1,233/1,259 backfilled rows left 3 dereferenced parquet objects (32,732 B), 3 index bundles (85,189 B), 4 catalog revisions, and HEAD.json that the post-abort catalog (generation 4) no longer references. A service restart and a subsequent GC pass (which correctly pruned `zephyr.stage`'s superseded catalogs 35→2) did not touch them. The 24 h orphan grace period had not elapsed at observation time, so re-check `gs://marin-us-central2/finelog/marin-dev/_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/` after 2026-08-30T23:15Z before treating retention as confirmed.

The retained HEAD is intentional (recovery recognizes the legacy-authority state and a later re-registration reuses the table directory), but the dereferenced data and index objects are bounded garbage per aborted migration. A sweep for tables whose durable state selects the legacy version — or routing them through the store-level orphan GC — would close it.

Part of the object-native storage rollout (#8737, PR #8748).

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Reproduce/locate the reported code path
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Root-cause analysis
- [x] Decide scope and hand off

The referenced code (`store/table/maintenance.rs`, `collect_objects`, object-backed tables) exists only on the branch of open PR [#8748](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8748) (`agent/20260827-fix-8737`); it is not on `main`. So this is a follow-up to in-flight work, not a `main`-based bug — no parallel PR. Analysis below is for folding into #8748.

**Research**

The GC gate is too strict. [`collect_objects` returns early](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/maintenance.rs#L312-L315) when [`is_object_backed()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/controller.rs#L207-L211) is false, and that predicate is `object_persistence_configured() && (spec_selects_objects || head_published)`. After an aborted spec migration the active definition reverts to the legacy version, so [`spec_selects_objects` refreshes to false](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/controller.rs#L234-L237); the table's own sweep then no-ops even though its `_finelog/tables/<table>/` objects from the migration are still on disk. Both maintenance branches already enqueue [`ObjectCollection`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/maintenance.rs#L207-L219), so the plumbing exists — only the predicate blocks the reverted table.

The store-level sweep it would call, [`run_gc_states` → `gc_obsolete_states`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L308-L346), only needs `require_objects()` and a resolvable HEAD; it keys off the current HEAD/state, prunes superseded revisions under `state_retention`/`orphan_grace`, and preserves the live HEAD — exactly the intended behavior for the post-abort (generation 4) authority. Note it short-circuits to `Ok(0)` when [`load()` returns `None`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L316-L318), and [`load()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L54-L94) returns `Some` whenever HEAD validates, independent of legacy-vs-object authority.

**Proposed fix (for #8748)**

Relax the `collect_objects` gate so a table that is object-persistence-configured and still owns residual object state under its directory is swept even when its active spec selects the legacy version — routing it through the existing `run_gc_states`/`gc_obsolete_states` path rather than adding a new sweeper. The fenced-writer guard already in `gc_obsolete_states` stays. Two things to confirm while implementing, since they decide whether relaxing the guard alone is sufficient: (1) whether the abort/recovery path keeps HEAD resolvable so `load()` returns the generation-4 state (if authority-revert makes `load()` return `None`, the store sweep also needs a residual-object path); (2) that pruning respects the intentional HEAD retention on a legacy-authority table. Add a regression test that migrates a table to objects, aborts mid-backfill, runs a maintenance cycle, and asserts dereferenced parquet/index/catalog objects are collected past the grace window while HEAD and the current state survive.

Caveat: the marin-dev observation is still provisional — the 24 h orphan grace had not elapsed, so re-check `gs://marin-us-central2/finelog/marin-dev/_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/` after 2026-08-30T23:15Z, per the issue, before treating the leak as confirmed rather than merely delayed.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Closing: the mechanism claim here was wrong, and the real defect it led to is now fixed on the PR branch.

The abort does not strand the table's GC. `is_object_backed()` stays true through the retained HEAD (`head_published` latches on the live server and `adopt_claimed` re-latches it on every boot), so the legacy maintenance cycle keeps dispatching `ObjectCollection` for the aborted table. marin-dev confirms it empirically: the three superseded catalog revisions were swept once the 1-hour retention window elapsed (only the current gen-4 catalog, HEAD, and the data/index objects still inside the 24-hour orphan grace remain at `_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/`).

Writing the regression test for this exposed the genuine bug adjacent to it: the orphan sweep walked only `objects/` and the referenced-key set collected only data-source IDs, so orphaned index bundles and covering-projection artifacts were never collected for any table. Fixed in 7d9b381997 (PR #8748): the reference set now keeps every object a retained state names, the sweep covers `objects/`, `indices/`, and `projections/`, and the test drives register → migrate → abort → GC and verifies only HEAD and the current catalog remain.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
The production `levanter.metrics` namespace carries a catalog segment row for the nested partitioned path `run_id/31/seg_L2_0000000000801962040.parquet` whose file does not exist on disk. Local segment adoption prunes the row's 59 sibling rows but leaves this one (the nested `run_id/31/` path shape appears to escape the reconciliation walk), and the legacy archive uploader then retries the upload every ~30 s forever:

```
WARN finelog::store::legacy::archive: legacy archive upload failed ... No such file or directory
```

Reproduced identically in both full-sample rehearsal rounds for #8748 against a copied production store (31 retries in a ~15 minute window, the only warning category present in an otherwise clean run). Pre-existing on main; unrelated to the object-native branch. Fix likely belongs in adoption's footer-reconciliation walk (treat a catalog row whose path contains partition subdirectories the same as a flat row when the file is absent) plus a retry backoff or tombstone for upload sources that arepermanently missing.

Found during the #8737 / PR #8748 rehearsals.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read the issue and check actionability
- [x] Locate the `finelog::store::legacy::archive` code and the reconciliation walk
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs / issues)
- [x] Decide scope: analysis comment vs PR

**Not a main-branch fix.** The `store::legacy::archive` module, `adopt_local_segments`, and the nested-partition L1+ layout the report describes exist only on the `agent/20260827-fix-8737` branch of the still-open [PR #8748](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8748); none of it is on `main` (`grep` for `legacy archive` / `store::legacy` across `main` returns nothing). So the "pre-existing on main" framing is off — this is a defect inside the object-native rework itself, and any fix lands on that PR's branch, not against `main`. Per the fix-issue duplicate-work rule I am not opening a parallel implementation PR over an open PR that owns this subsystem.

**Research.** The recurring `No such file or directory` warning is `legacy upload read failed`: archive `sync()` walks every `L>=1` `LOCAL` catalog row and `tokio::fs::read`s the file; a row pointing at an absent file sets `all_durable = false` and is retried on every ~30s sync, forever, with no backoff or tombstone ([archive.rs sync/read](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/legacy/archive.rs#L82-L114)). Adoption pass 1 is supposed to prune exactly this: a `LOCAL` catalog row whose file is gone is dropped via `remove_segment` ([adopt.rs pass 1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/adopt.rs#L641-L657)). Removal keys purely on whether `row.path` is present in `local_files`, and `local_files` comes from a recursive `discover_segments` walk that does descend partition subdirectories ([segment.rs discover](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/segment.rs#L620-L677)) — so a `LOCAL` row with a missing nested file *should* be pruned, which is why the surviving `run_id/31/…` row is surprising.

The most likely escape is a `row.path` string mismatch: `local_files` is keyed by `discover_segments`' `to_string_lossy()` path, and the phantom row survives only if its stored path fails to match that keying (normalization / absolute-vs-relative for the nested partition shape), or if its `location` is `BOTH` rather than `LOCAL` (pass 1 would then collapse it to `REMOTE`, not remove it — yet archive sync only reads `LOCAL` rows, so that alone would not produce the warning). I could not confirm which without the copied production store from the rehearsal.

**Proposed approach (for #8748, two independent defenses):**
1. Reconciliation: make adoption prune a phantom nested-partition `LOCAL` row the same as a flat one. The concrete check is whether the catalog `path` for the `run_id/31/seg_L2_*.parquet` row matches the string `discover_segments` produces for that same physical file — if they diverge, normalize both sides to one canonical form before the `local_files` lookup at [adopt.rs L641-L643](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/adopt.rs#L641-L657). A regression test: seed a catalog `LOCAL` row under `ns/31/seg_L2_*.parquet` with no file on disk, run `adopt_local_segments`, assert the row is removed.
2. Archive sync: give a `LOCAL` upload source whose local read fails `NotFound` a backoff or a tombstone so it stops retrying every 30s, rather than logging forever ([archive.rs L96-L102](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/legacy/archive.rs#L96-L102)).

**To confirm root cause**, please share for the surviving `run_id/31/seg_L2_0000000000801962040.parquet` row: its exact catalog `path` string and `location`, and the path string `discover_segments` yields for the sibling flat rows that *were* pruned. That pins whether the fix belongs in reconciliation path-matching, the row's location handling, or both.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Fixed on the #8748 branch in b0928158df. `localize_source` now distinguishes definitive absence (no local file and an archive miss) from transient failure, and a version-0 import drops such a row instead of retrying it: the restated backfill universe stops owing rows nothing holds, the import completes, and the catalog row that feeds the 30-second upload retry loop is deleted. A regression test reproduces the production shape (a `run_id/31/seg_L2_….parquet` LOCAL row with no bytes anywhere) and verifies the import activates with the row gone.

For `levanter.metrics` specifically, the retry noise ends when the table goes through its object-native migration, which removes the phantom row as an unrecoverable source. This closes with PR #8748.

The `cw-tas` ClusterQueue sets `preemption.withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority`, but quota is deliberately non-binding ("the pressure signal is TAS, not quota" — `lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py`), and on the deployed Kueue version TAS lack-of-fit does not appear to trigger within-queue preemption. The install script itself flags TAS-aware preemption as version-sensitive. Net effect: interactive submissions queue behind batch instead of reclaiming, which contradicts the intended band semantics.

A second interaction worsens it: when TAS finally admits, it pins the pod to one hostname via node affinity from its capacity snapshot; a concurrently admitted gang can take that node's GPU first, leaving the pod `Unschedulable` (`1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 64 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity`). Iris correctly returns the task to PENDING, but the fresh attempt re-enters the same non-preempting queue.

Reproduce:
1. Fill a TAS cluster's GPUs with batch-band Iris jobs.
2. Submit a small interactive-band GPU job.
3. Observe it gated indefinitely with the TAS fit message and no preemption events.

Expected: an interactive-band workload preempts batch-band workloads when TAS cannot fit it, per the documented band semantics.

Observed job: `/power/curriculum-rl-r2-cleanup/eval-20260829-200348-power-curriculum-rl-grade-adaptive-76e2` (inference task events show the full sequence). Marin-side mitigation for the resulting eval deaths is in #8769 (startup timeout no longer consumed by queue time).

Done when:
TAS-driven lack-of-fit for a higher-band workload triggers preemption of lower-band pods (validated on the deployed Kueue version, e.g. via the kind smoke), or the ClusterQueue configuration is changed so band priority is enforced through binding quota.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis** (not opening a PR — the fix is version-sensitive and its definition of done requires validation on the deployed Kueue, larger than a self-contained change).

**Root cause.** The `cw-tas` ClusterQueue asks Kueue for priority preemption via [`preemption.withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L363-L377), but every resource carries a sentinel [`NON_BINDING_QUOTA`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L114-L123) so quota never binds. Kueue's within-queue preemption selects victims by whether reclaiming their *quota* would admit the pending Workload; with non-binding quota there is never quota pressure, so the only blocker is the TAS topology fit — and on the deployed Kueue the TAS assigner reports lack-of-fit without feeding back into preemption. The higher-band Workload gets `QuotaReserved` but no victims, and its pods stay `SchedulingGated`. The install script already [flags this as version-sensitive](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py#L51-L54).

The secondary interaction (node-affinity pin from a stale TAS capacity snapshot losing a race to a concurrently-admitted gang → `Unschedulable` → Iris returns the task to PENDING → re-enters the same non-preempting queue) is a consequence of the same missing preemption, not an independent bug.

**Two viable directions (the DoD names both):**

1. **Make TAS lack-of-fit drive preemption.** This depends entirely on the deployed cks-kueue version and its TAS-preemption support; the feature-gate set is [`CKS_KUEUE_FEATURE_GATES`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L52-L59) and the coreweave variant pins no chart version (`latest`). First step is to read the running version (`helm list -n kueue-system`, controller image tag) and check upstream Kueue's TAS-preemption support/gate for it. If a newer chart or gate is required, that is a chart upgrade + gate change, validated by extending the kind smoke ([`gpu_gang_smoke.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/tests/e2e/gpu_gang_smoke.py), which has no preemption case today) with a batch-fills-cluster → interactive-preempts scenario.

2. **Enforce band priority through binding quota** on the scarce accelerator resources (`nvidia.com/gpu`, `rdma/ib`) only, leaving cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage non-binding. Binding GPU quota restores the classic, well-supported preemption path (quota pressure → within-queue `LowerPriority` eviction) without waiting on TAS-preemption. The cost is that GPU quota now has to track real capacity, which fights the "autoscaler is the capacity authority, Kueue never rejects on quota" design the comments call out — so it needs the quota kept in sync with scale-group max slices.

**Recommendation before implementation:** confirm the deployed cks-kueue version and whether it supports TAS-driven within-queue preemption (this decides between directions 1 and 2), and confirm the priority values in [`IRIS_PRIORITY_CLASSES`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/types.py#L37-L41) (interactive=10 > batch=0) are the intended reclaim ordering. Either path must ship with a preemption case in the kind smoke as the acceptance gate. Marin-side eval mitigation is already tracked in #8769.

comments.body:
🤖
**Research**

CoreWeave Pulumi pins [cks-kueue 1.4.0](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/coreweave/kueue.py), which contains Kueue 0.18.0; the kind smoke also pins [upstream 0.18.0](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py). ## TL;DR

Just kicking off: measure whether adaptive environment/problem sampling improves RL training efficiency under a fixed compute budget, versus uniform random sampling.

## Description

We run SkyRL GRPO post-training on a small Qwen policy (0.6B class) over a pool of verifiable, non-agentic environments (math datasets spanning difficulty, plus simple programmatic tasks). Each arm uses the same model, data pool, and budget; only the policy for choosing which environment/problem to roll out next differs.

Arms:

1. Naive sampling: uniform random over the pool (baseline).
2. Modified Thompson sampling: bias toward environments currently yielding reward signal (e.g. per-env reward variance / pass-rate entropy), with decay so the belief tracks policy drift.
3. Pre-graded difficulty (problems graded 0–N easiest→hardest):
   - Naive curriculum: 1/N of budget per level.
   - Adaptive curriculum: train on a level until it stops paying (saturated or not learning), then move.
   - Biased sampling: grades seed an initial belief distribution for the Thompson sampler.

Budget: fixed output-token count per run, falling back to GPU wall-time (64 H100s x fixed hours) if token accounting is impractical. Runs use INTERACTIVE priority on cw-rno2a. The experiment is wired through Marin artifact steps (`marin.rl.skyrl`) so arms are cached and rerunnable; sampler support lands on a MarinSkyRL branch if the pinned trainer lacks the hooks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reward-signal-aware sampling concentrates rollouts where the learning signal is, so adaptive arms should reach a given eval score with fewer output tokens than uniform sampling. Quantify the value of each mechanism at fixed budget.

The curriculum sampler is implemented on MarinSkyRL branch [`curriculum-sampling`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/curriculum-sampling) (@2a9034fd) and validated live: naive, thompson, and grade-adaptive smoke arms all ran green end-to-end (train → HF export → eval) on cw-rno2a.

🤖 **Final report: efficacy and recommendations.**

**Conclusions.**
1. *Curriculum value here is token efficiency, not a better endpoint.* At a fixed generated-token budget (146M), grade-adaptive reached mid-run-baseline quality at ~53% of naive's token spend (val-math500 0.156 vs 0.080), with thompson close behind (0.140). 2. *Thompson sampling is the best no-prep default.* No offline grading required, decay handles policy drift, competitive under both budget definitions, and it visibly reallocated: bins with zero informative groups (MATH L5, AIME — all-fail for a 0.6B policy) dropped to the 1% floor.
3. *Grade-prior and grade-uniform added little* — the grade-derived prior washes out once real reward evidence accumulates, and fixed 1/N allocation wastes budget on uninformative extremes.

**Recommendations.**
- Re-run naive / thompson / grade-adaptive at 3 seeds for error bars before production conclusions (~$3 × current spend; each arm is 64 GPUs × 1.75 h).
- Extend grade-adaptive to 300+ steps so it traverses all grades; its curve was still rising at half the token budget.
- Make thompson difficulty-directional (distinguish all-pass from all-fail groups) — that should recover grade-adaptive's token efficiency without pre-grading.
- Batch-level uninformative-group resampling (DAPO-style) is complementary to bin-level sampling and likely stacks.

comments.body:
🤖 # Round 2 final report: DAPO, procedural bins, and directional samplers

All seven arms completed: 120 GRPO steps each on 64 H100s (cw-rno2a, Qwen3-0.6B, batch 512×8 samples, non-thinking, ~1024-token generations). Every arm shares the same expanded pool and differs only in prompt sampling and (for the DAPO variants) group filtering. Terminal evals are Evalchemy MATH500 and GSM8K-0shot against the exported step-120 checkpoint; in-run validation is scored by the training environments on held-out slices.

## Results

| arm | generated tokens | in-run val (all) | MATH500 | GSM8K-0shot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| naive | 203M | 0.513 | 0.362 | 0.390 |
| thompson | 149M | 0.480 | 0.350 | 0.409 |
| learnability | 220M | 0.537 | 0.418 | 0.444 |
| grade-adaptive | 130M | 0.534 | 0.346 | 0.439 |
| grade-prior (directional) | 211M | 0.487 | 0.408 | 0.418 |
| naive-dapo | 190M | 0.555 | 0.414 | 0.401 |
| **thompson-dapo** | 205M | **0.571** | **0.434** | **0.456** |

Token totals include work redone after preemption-driven restarts (real spend). Round-2 numbers are not comparable to round 1: the pool now spends a large share of budget on procedural bins, which lowers math transfer for every arm equally (round-1 naive hit 0.460 MATH500 on the math-only pool).

![score vs tokens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/all-tokens.png)
![score vs steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/all-steps.png)

MATH500 and GSM8K validation trajectories against token spend:

![val-math500 vs tokens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/val-math500-tokens.png)
![val-gsm8k vs tokens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/val-gsm8k-tokens.png)

## Grading mechanism and distributions

Grades place all 13 bins on one 0–10 scale from two sources. Math bins take grades from **source metadata**: GSM8K at 1, MATH levels 1–2/3/4/5 at 2/4/6/8, AIME at 10. Procedural reasoning-gym bins take **a-priori grades from generator knobs**, assigned before any model saw a sample: chain_sum at grades 0/3/7 (2 terms 1–2 digits → 5–6 terms 4 digits signed), spell_backward at 5/9 (3–5 vs 8–10 letters), base_conversion at 5/9 (bases 2–10 values ≤500 vs bases 11–16). Train pool: 18,619 rows (gsm8k 2000, math-l12 1911, math-l3 1590, math-l4 1690, math-l5 2296, aime 932, 7 procedural bins × 1200); validation adds 128-row held-out generator draws per procedural family.

How well did the grades predict reality? Realized pass rates from the learnability arm:

| bin (grade) | pass rate @ step 10 | @ step 120 |
|---|---|---|
| rg-sum-easy (0) | 0.97 | 1.00 |
| gsm8k (1) | 0.49 | 0.84 |
| math-l12 (2) | 0.53 | 0.84 |
| rg-sum-med (3) | 0.97 | 0.99 |
| math-l3 (4) | 0.41 | 0.70 |
| rg-spell-short (5) | 0.82 | 1.00 |
| rg-base-small (5) | 0.58 | 0.90 |
| math-l4 (6) | 0.28 | 0.57 |
| rg-sum-hard (7) | 0.74 | 0.90 |
| math-l5 (8) | 0.07 | 0.27 |
| rg-base-large (9) | 0.26 | 0.96 |
| rg-spell-long (9) | 0.79 | 0.97 |
| aime (10) | 0.00 | 0.06 |

Two clear findings. **Within a family, metadata grades rank difficulty essentially perfectly** (math: 0.53 → 0.41 → 0.28 → 0.07 → 0.004 down the levels). **Across families, knob-derived grades misjudged absolute difficulty badly**: arithmetic chains are near-trivial for Qwen3-0.6B at any knob setting we chose, and spelling/base-conversion saturate within ~10 steps once the model learns the answer format — procedural tasks measure format acquisition more than reasoning. The pre-registered grades were wrong in exactly the way a real practitioner's would be, which made this a fair test of whether samplers recover from miscalibrated priors.

## Sampling mechanisms

- **naive** — the stock uniform shuffle without replacement. Control.
- **thompson** — Beta Thompson sampling on each bin's decayed *informative-group fraction* (a GRPO group is informative when its rewards are not all equal), decay 0.95, 5% probability floor. Round 1's design.
- **learnability** (new) — Thompson draw on each bin's decayed per-sample *pass rate*, weighted by p·(1−p), which peaks at 50% solve rate. Motivated by round 1's core diagnosis: informative-fraction cannot distinguish a too-easy bin from a too-hard one (both produce uniform groups), so it has no direction.
- **grade-prior** (redesigned) — learnability with grade-seeded Beta priors: prior mean pass rate falls linearly from 0.85 at the easiest grade to 0.05 at the hardest, with 8 pseudo-counts. Round 1's undirected-optimism version collapsed to thompson within ~20 steps; this version encodes the grade as a belief about *pass rate*, which the p·(1−p) weighting turns into "start in the middle band."
- **grade-adaptive** — a level pointer walking the grade ladder, advancing when the current level stops producing informative signal; 20% exploration mass off-level.
- **DAPO filter** (`naive-dapo`, `thompson-dapo`) — drop zero-advantage groups after generation and keep drawing batches until a full informative batch accumulates (the standard DAPO dynamic-sampling recipe). The curriculum sampler updates on raw pre-filter batches so filtering does not bias its statistics.

Weight trajectories show the directional machinery working as designed. Learnability zeroes the saturated procedural bins almost immediately, holds AIME near the floor, and walks its mass up the math ladder as the model improves (math-l3/l4 dominate late). Grade-prior starts mid-band per its prior, then evidence overrides the miscalibrated procedural placements within ~15 steps:

![learnability weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/curriculum-learnability-weight.png)
![grade-prior weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/assets/curriculum-rl-r2/curriculum-grade-prior-weight.png)

## Analysis

1. **DAPO is the single biggest win.** thompson-dapo leads every metric, and both DAPO arms beat their non-DAPO counterparts at *equal token spend*, not just equal steps — filtering converts budget that would fund zero-gradient groups into informative ones. The score-vs-tokens chart shows the DAPO curves rising fastest through the whole budget range.
2. **Direction matters more than curriculum-ness.** Learnability (0.418/0.444) beats thompson (0.350/0.409) decisively — same Thompson machinery, better signal. Plain thompson was the weakest arm, confirming round 1's suspicion that informative-fraction is a compass without a needle.
3. **Grades survive contact with reality only where they were right.** Grade-prior recovered from its miscalibrated procedural priors but paid an early-budget tax for them, landing between thompson and learnability. With honest grades (the math family) the ordering is genuinely useful; with guessed grades the evidence-driven samplers simply relearn the truth and the prior contributes little. Grading effort is only worth what the grader knows.
4. **Grade-adaptive remains the token-efficiency champion** (0.534 val-all on 130M tokens, ~64% of naive's spend), echoing round 1. Its focused single-level sampling generates shorter, more solvable rollouts.
5. **Procedural tasks are cheap curriculum filler but weak transfer vehicles.** They gave the samplers real difficulty structure to exploit and clean val curves (e.g. base-conversion 0.26→0.96), but every arm's MATH500 dropped versus round 1's math-only pool. At 0.6B, budget spent on spelling does not buy math.

## Conclusions and future work

At fixed budget, the value ranking is: DAPO filtering > directional (pass-rate) sampling > adaptive level curricula > grade priors > informative-fraction sampling. The obvious composition — **learnability + DAPO** — was not run this round and is the first follow-up: the mechanisms are orthogonal (what to sample vs what to keep) and their gains plausibly stack.

Future work, in priority order:
- **learnability-dapo arm** at the same budget point.
- **Measured grades over guessed grades**: a ~1-hour pre-pass scoring k samples per bin with the base model would have produced a nearly perfect prior for free; grade-prior with measured priors is the honest test of "grades as belief."
- **Token-budget-equalized stopping** (stop every arm at, say, 150M generated tokens) to remove the step/token conflation entirely.
- **A model one size up** (4–8B, thinking mode) where AIME-band bins are learnable and the grade ladder has more headroom.
- Infra hardening from this round is tracked separately: #8774 (gang restart after head preemption, in progress), #8781/#8782 (TAS priority preemption, merged), plus the eval endpoint queue-time fix and TTL-routed Ray session logs in #8769.

Experiment code and pins are in #8769 (`experiments/post_training/curriculum_rl/`, MarinSkyRL `curriculum-sampling` @ `4a1f99fc`). Charts regenerate with `report_charts.py`; per-bin stats with `report_pool_stats.py`; terminal scores with `report_evals.py`.

New `learnability-dapo` and `grade-prior-dapo` arms compose the round-2 winners; the pool adds val-amc (grade 9) and val-theoremqa (grade 13) so the grade-weighted end metric (weights ∝ 1+grade, never shown to the sampler) sees the ladder top.

Now running at `2026.08.31`:
- **Qwen3-0.6B, 6 arms** on cw-rno2a (120 steps each): naive, naive-dapo, learnability-dapo, grade-prior-dapo, grade-adaptive, grade-prior.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Round-3 finding: adaptive sampling is fragile to reward-contract mismatch; grade priors buy robustness.

The snowball-learnability-dapo arm showed val-gsm8k pass@1 = 0.000 at step 10 while snowball-naive scored 0.891 from the same base model — with learnability simultaneously beating naive on harder bins (MATH-500 0.66 vs 0.63). Retained trajectories pin the cause: Snowball answers gsm8k correctly but in its SFT style (`\boxed{300}`), while the gsm8k environment's rule grader only accepts the answer after `"####"`, so every rollout scores 0. The bin's zero pass rate measures format compliance, not ability.

The three samplers then diverge exactly along their designs:

- **naive** samples gsm8k uniformly (~54 rollouts/step); rare rollouts that happen to emit `####` get positive advantage and RL teaches the format within 10 steps → val 0.891.
- **learnability + group-informative weighting** observes pass = 0 at step 1, assigns the bin near-floor weight (0.009 vs ~0.09 for active bins), starves it, and never learns the format → val 0.000.
- **grade-prior + group-informative** keeps sampling on its grade-3 prior (9 informative groups by step 9, pass EMA 0.16 → 0.33) and recovers → val 0.828 at step 10.

Letting the arms run to 60 steps as-is: the dynamics are the experiment. For the report, the snowball headline metric will be shown with and without val-gsm8k, since the bin conflates format with difficulty for this model. Follow-up recommendation: normalize every pool bin to one answer contract (`\boxed{}` + math-verify) so grades measure difficulty only, and add cold-start optimism or a re-exploration floor to pure-feedback samplers so an observed-zero bin is revisited often enough to distinguish "too hard" from "mis-specified".

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
## Leonardo non-agentic RL throughput results — gsm8k GRPO (short) + MATH (long-CoT)

Results from the MarinSkyRL throughput ablations on Leonardo. Methodology is "measure the per-step timing breakdown from the run logs, sweep one knob at a time, compare on **effective tokens/s** for work-changing cells and **sec/step** for work-fixed cells."

### Constraints & hparams

**Hardware / stack**
- CINECA Leonardo, **A100-64GB** (4/node; NVLink intra-node, InfiniBand inter-node). 64 GB/GPU is the binding VRAM limit; no compute-node internet; rotating keys.
- MarinSkyRL (`skyrl-train`): FSDP2 policy + vLLM rollout, **`colocate_all=true`**, `run_engines_locally=true`, NCCL policy→engine weight sync, `use_kl_loss=false`. Synchronous path (gen and train do **not** overlap).

**gsm8k grid base** — Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, GRPO. Canary: `train_batch_size=32` · `n_samples_per_prompt=4` · `gpu_memory_utilization=0.70` · `enforce_eager=true` · 4 engines × TP1 · `micro_*_batch_size_per_gpu=8` · `max_generate_length=512`. Reference: **9.58 s/step** (233-step epoch).

**MATH (long-CoT) base** — Hendrycks MATH L3–5 (5,582 train) + MATH-500 val; Minerva boxed-answer **±1 reward**; `train_batch_size=64` · `n_samples=4` · `max_generate_length=4096` · CUDA graphs ON. Natural CoT (~600–660 tok), no forced EOS.

**Protocol** — 25-step runs; warm-mean over steps 6–25 (first 5 discarded). Reward is *not* converged at 25 steps, so **entropy stability** (~0.36, no collapse everywhere) is the correctness guard, not absolute reward.

### gsm8k 1.5B throughput grid (18 cells)

- **CUDA graphs (`enforce_eager=false`) is the standout near-free win: −29% sec/step (9.61 → 6.81), generation −50% (5.73 → 2.89 s).** Should be ON always.
- **Wider rollout batch (`train_batch_size` × `n_samples`) scales effective tokens/s** by filling the otherwise-starved generator. Best balance: `combo_C` (tbs128·n8·gmu0.85·cudagraph·micro16) = **12,882 eff tok/s @ 20.7 s/step**. Max throughput: `max_width` (tbs512…) = **15,231 eff tok/s** but 70.7 s/step.
- **The bottleneck MIGRATES with width.** At base width the canary is **generation-bound (gen 60%) AND the generator is starved** (KV cache usage 0.0–0.3%, "Running" 1–6 of a 1.3M-token cache). Beyond ~tbs128, **`policy_train` compute becomes the wall** (tbs256 50%, combo_D 56%, max_width 58%) while generation stays ~6–16 s and KV stays <11%. It is **never memory-bound** (max_width peaked 10.2% KV; the only "ceiling" was *dataset exhaustion* — epochs=1 × 7,473 rows ÷ tbs512 = 14 steps).
- **Layout:** 4×TP1 > 2×TP2 > 1×TP4 for the 1.5B; colocated > disaggregated at 4 GPU.

### Multi-node generator scaling (batch fixed at 2,048 seqs; scale engines = 4×nodes)

| nodes | engines | sec/step | gen-frac | policy_train-frac | sync_weights s | eff tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 36.9 | 24.3% | 55.7% | 1.05 | 14,435 |
| 2 | 8 | 73.7 | 8.6% | 68.4% | 2.40 | 7,222 |
| 4 | 16 | 46.6 | 10.5% | 62.1% | 3.63 | 11,394 |
| 8 | 32 | 35.9 | 12.3% | 51.1% | 6.33 | 14,838 |

**gsm8k/1.5B is never generation-bound — zero extra engines help.** 1→2 nodes is a sharp regression (cross-node FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter on a tiny 1.5B doesn't amortize); 8 nodes only *breaks even* with 1 node. New monotonic limiter at scale = `sync_weights` (NCCL broadcast grows with engine count).

### Model-size saturation on a real long-CoT task (MATH), single node 4×A100-64GB

| model | parallelism | sec/step | gen-frac | policy_train-frac | avg gen tok | reward (±1) | OOM? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 28.3 | **0.52** | 0.35 | 609 | −0.95 (~2% pass) | ok |
| 3B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 41.7 | 0.47 | 0.40 | 663 | −0.81 | ok |
| 7B | FSDP4 + 4×TP1 | 68.4 | 0.45 | 0.42 | 659 | −0.13 | ok |
| 14B | FSDP4 + 2×TP2 | 100.9 | **0.32** | **0.53** | 612 | ~0.00 (~50% pass) | ok |
| 32B | FSDP4 + 1×TP4 | — | — | — | — | — | **OOM ceiling** |

- **Direction flip vs the naive guess:** on a real long-CoT task the **small end is generation-bound** (1.5B gen-frac 0.52) — opposite of short-gsm8k. As size grows the system becomes **more train-bound** (FSDP fwd+bwd scales superlinearly with params); **crossover is 7B↔14B**.
- Reward rises monotonically with size (~2% → ~50% MATH pass). **32B OOMs single-node** (cleared vLLM init but OOM'd in the FSDP backward) → needs multi-node / disaggregated.

### Bigger models, multi-node (MATH)
- **Qwen3-32B (dense): TRAINS on 2 nodes / 8 GPU** — FSDP (cpu_offload + gradient_checkpointing), vLLM 4×TP2 (TP1 OOMs), gmu 0.75, `max_model_len=8192`. ~1,534 s/step, **policy_train 71%** (gen-frac **0.19** — the train-bound trend continues: 1.5B 0.52 → 14B 0.32 → 32B 0.19).
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE):** EP trainer path works end-to-end (grouped-GEMM + router-replay; `torchtitan` installed, zero stack conflict), but OOMs at the colocated full-weight `broadcast_to_inference_engines` → also needs multi-node / disaggregated weight-sync.

### Context-length stress (Qwen2.5-7B; workload fixed at prompt 1024 / gen 4096; only `max_model_len` grows)

| max_model_len | vLLM max-concurrency | sec/step | gen-frac | KV% pk | OOM? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16k | 38.9× | 68.6 | 0.46 | 4.2 | ok |
| 32k | 19.5× | 71.4 | 0.47 | 4.1 | ok |
| 65k | 9.7× | 69.8 | 0.47 | 4.2 | ok |
| 131k | 4.9× | 70.5 | 0.47 | 4.1 | ok |

**No context ceiling to 131k on 4×A100-64GB** (KV pool constant ~638k tok / 34 GiB @ gmu 0.85; max-concurrency halves cleanly per doubling; throughput flat ~70 s/step). **Caveat:** this is a KV-*capacity* test — the ~660-tok CoT never fills the window; a true long-context test needs a long-**input** task (repo-level / long-doc), where realized concurrency would collapse toward ~1 and the actual ceiling would appear.

### Takeaways for Leonardo non-agentic RL
1. **Single-node throughput recipe:** `enforce_eager=false` + `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85` + wide batch (tbs128–256 × n8) + `micro_train_batch_size_per_gpu=16` → ~13–15k eff tok/s at 1.5B. (Raise `epochs` for wide-tbs so runs aren't capped by dataset exhaustion.)
2. **Generation-boundedness is a function of (model size, CoT length), not batch alone:** small models + long CoT → generation dominates (added generators pay off); large models / short outputs → train-bound (levers are train-side micro-batch/sharding + the structural **fully-async** overlap, which is the biggest untapped win and not yet exploited here).
3. **64 GB/GPU is the real ceiling** for ≥32B colocated long-context RL → multi-node / disaggregated (offload inference off the training GPUs).

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 *(posted by an agent on behalf of @penfever)*

## OPD grid results — on-policy distillation (Qwen3-32B teacher → Qwen3-1.7B student), gsm8k, Leonardo

Companion to the pure-RL throughput grid above. **OPD** = on-policy distillation: the student (Qwen3-1.7B) generates rollouts via vLLM; per-token reward = −KL(student‖teacher) over the student's own tokens (`advantage_estimator=no_op`, `policy_loss_type=importance_sampling`, `use_kl_in_reward=true`). FSDP ref worker = KL teacher; a separate vLLM-served **Qwen3-32B** supplies top-K logprobs. No env reward. Non-agentic, local gsm8k parquet. Base: 2 nodes × 4 A100-64GB, teacher TP2 + student 1.7B FSDP2 + 4× colocated vLLM TP1.

**Structural finding:** OPD is **teacher-score-bound — 90–97% of every step** is the 32B teacher scoring rollout tokens (`prompt_logprobs=top_k` over every response token). Student generate (8–24 s) and train (38–91 s) are noise. So the speed levers all act on teacher scoring; convergence is governed separately by lr.

### Batch 1 — speed (one knob off base; warm-mean steps 5–15)
| cell | knob vs base | sec/step | teacher-score % | KL Δ (run) | note |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **base** | topk128·lr1e-5·tbs64·n8·gen1024·TP2·eager | 1461 | 95.7% | −0.022 | reference |
| **topk32** | top_k=32 | **532** | 89.5% | −0.023 | **2.74× faster, KL-Δ unharmed** |
| topk64 | top_k=64 | 834 | 93.0% | **−0.028** | best Batch-1 KL-Δ |
| topk256 | top_k=256 | 2663 | 97.3% | −0.018 | 1.82× slower, *worst* total Δ |
| teacherTP4 | teacher TP4 | 1401 | 95.5% | −0.026 | ≈ base — teacher scoring not TP-bound (non-lever) |
| tbs128 | train_batch=128 | 2899 | 95.9% | −0.030 | ~2× tokens → ~2× wall; eff tok/s flat (anti-lever) |
| gen512 | max_gen=512 | 796 | 93.9% | −0.036 | −46% step (halves scored tokens); diff operating point |
| cudagraph | enforce_eager=false | 1446 | 95.8% | −0.027 | no win (student gen <2% of step) |

**top_k is THE speed knob** (superlinear: each doubling ≈1.6–1.85× cost) **and convergence does not scale with it** — k=32–64 captures the bulk of teacher mass for this pair, so cheap top_k loses ~nothing in KL descent. teacherTP4 / cudagraph are non-levers here; tbs128 is anti. Entropy healthy everywhere (0.18→0.29–0.35, no collapse).

### Batch 2 — convergence (one knob off base; 8h wall ≈16 steps)
| cell | lr | n_samp | steps | KL first→last (Δ) | pass@k last | sec/step | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|---|
| lr3e6 | 3e-6 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→0.337 (−0.020) | p@8 **0.03** | 1428 | lr too low — no task learning (≈ base lr1e-5) |
| **lr3e5** | 3e-5 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→0.313 (**−0.043**) | p@8 **0.75** | 1417 | **WINNER** — pass@8 0.03→0.75; entropy/grad healthy |
| lr1e4 | 1e-4 | 8 | 16 | 0.357→**5.59** (+5.23) | p@8 0.39 | 1415 | **diverges** (KL spike 19, grad 21) — too aggressive |
| n4 | 1e-5 | 4 | 16 | 0.366→0.334 (−0.031) | p@4 0.34 | **723** | cheapest (2× steps/hr), higher-variance, still descends |
| n16 | 1e-5 | 16 | 10/12 ⛔TIMEOUT | 0.360→0.343 (−0.017) | p@16 0.59 | 2843 | lowest-variance; killed by 8h wall (partial accepted) |

**lr — not top_k — is the dominant convergence lever; knee at lr=3e-5.** Batch-1's flat KL descent + stuck pass@8 (~0.03) was an lr=1e-5 artifact: at lr=3e-5 the *same* config doubles KL-Δ and lifts gsm8k pass@8 0.03→0.75 (first cell to actually learn the task). lr=3e-6 ≈ no movement; lr=1e-4 diverges. lr and top_k are **orthogonal** (lr = whether it converges; top_k = teacher-mass fidelity per second).

### combo_opt — confirmation (`lr=3e-5 · top_k=64 · n8 · gen1024`, 16 steps)
- **pass@8 0.75–0.78** — matches the lr3e-5 winner (full convergence)
- **KL Δ ≈ −0.05** — best clean KL-Δ of the whole grid
- **832 s/step — ~1.7× faster** than the lr3e-5 cell (topk128, 1417 s/step), entropy healthy 0.30

Confirms orthogonality: top_k=64 keeps lr3e-5's convergence at 1.7× the speed.

### Recommended production OPD config (grid closed 2026-06-07)
**`lr=3e-5 · top_k=64 · n_samples=8 · gen=1024 · teacher TP2 · cudagraph off`** → gsm8k pass@8 ~0.75–0.78, KL-Δ ~−0.05, ~832 s/step (2 nodes / 8×A100). lr is the dominant convergence lever (knee at 3e-5), top_k=32–64 the cheap near-lossless speed lever, n_samples a clean speed×variance trade.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 *(posted by an agent on behalf of @penfever)*

## Analysis — best RL vs best OPD (RESOLVED by the cross-grids)

> **Updated 2026-06-08.** This supersedes the original "RL has only a throughput result, the comparison is still owed" framing. The two cross-grids — [RL accuracy + OPD throughput](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218#issuecomment-4647852428) — have now run, so the head-to-head is no longer owed; it's answered.

**Verdict (gsm8k, ~1.5–1.7B student): pure RL beats OPD on accuracy *and* on compute-to-accuracy.**

| | accuracy (pass@8) | speed | converges in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RL** — combo_acc(_stab), lr1e-5+n8+gen1024 | **~0.95–0.97** (≈task ceiling) | ~24–50 s/step | ~80–380 steps |
| **RL** — `base_q3`, **matched Qwen3-1.7B**, lr1e-6 | **0.94 peak** / 0.81 final | ~34 s/step | ~260 steps |
| **OPD** — base / topk16 (Qwen3-1.7B ← 32B) | ~0.82–0.83 (top3) | 836 → **387** s/step | ~16 steps |

On the **same student (Qwen3-1.7B), same task**, RL reaches **~0.94+** vs OPD's **~0.82**, while running **~10–20× cheaper per step** (≈19–50 s vs 387–836 s) — RL does ~40–70× more steps/hr. So both the accuracy ceiling and the pass@8-per-GPU-hour axis go to RL here.

**Why OPD loses the ceiling:** OPD distills toward the **Qwen3-32B teacher's distribution**, so its ceiling is the teacher — and 16 steps of distillation tops out at ~0.82–0.83. Pure RL is not teacher-bounded: gsm8k is small and **solvable from env reward**, so the policy climbs to the task ceiling (~1.0) on its own. A strong teacher doesn't help once the student can just solve the task. (Confirmed structurally by the OPD throughput grid: the **8B teacher fails the guard (0.578)** — a weaker teacher *lowers* the ceiling; teacher-size floor is >8B.)

**Mechanistic findings that fell out:**
- **GRPO lr knee = 1e-5**, two orders above OPD's distillation knee (3e-5). lr is the dominant lever in both, but the loss geometry differs.
- RL's near-ceiling result needs the **lr1e-5 × gen1024 combo** (neither alone clears 0.79) and an **entropy bonus** to avoid the collapse-to-0.04 that the bare lr1e-5 run shows. combo_acc_stab = ~0.95–0.98 *without* collapse.
- OPD is **93% teacher-forward-bound**; the only speed lever that paid is **top_k** (topk16 = 2.2× faster, lossless).

**Caveats — where this verdict does and doesn't hold:**
1. **Regime-specific.** gsm8k is small and saturable. The earlier MATH model-size sweep showed RL accuracy is *far* from ceiling at small sizes on harder math — on tasks the student **can't** solve from env reward alone, the 32B teacher signal (OPD) could still matter. This result is "small model, short-CoT, solvable task."
2. **Metric.** OPD pass@8 is a top-3-checkpoint mean; RL is last/peak. The ~0.94 vs ~0.82 gap dwarfs that difference, but they're not an identical estimator.
3. **OPD's biggest cost lever was never run.** Disaggregated teacher serving (teacher off the training GPUs) is deferred in the throughput grid — it would lower OPD's per-step cost, but it must close a ~10–20× gap to change the ranking, and it does nothing for the accuracy ceiling.

**Net:** for non-agentic gsm8k reasoning on Leonardo at this scale, **learning from env reward beats distilling a 32B teacher**, at lower compute. The open question OPD could still win is the harder-task / can't-solve-from-reward regime — that's the comparison worth running next, not another gsm8k pass.

---

### Grid A — RL accuracy grid (gsm8k GRPO, Qwen2.5-1.5B, 1×4 A100-64GB)

**Goal:** the GRPO config that maximizes **gsm8k pass@8**, run **to a plateau** (not a 25-step probe). Metric = pass@8 (same eval harness as OPD) + **pass@8 per GPU-hour**; entropy/grad_norm as stability guard.

**Goal:** maximize OPD **throughput** (sec/step, steps/hr, **pass@8 per GPU-hour**) **while holding the converged accuracy** — re-optimize speed *around the accuracy optimum*, with **pass@8 ~0.75 as a HARD GUARD on every cell** (a cell that speeds up but drops pass@8 below ~0.70 is a *failed* speed cell).

(The RL grid's gen/train levers are irrelevant here — student gen/train is <10% of the step.)

**20 cells, 2 batches:**
- **Batch 1 — teacher-serving + teacher-cost levers:** `base`, **`disagg`** (teacher on dedicated GPUs — biggest untapped lever, removes teacher↔student contention) + `disagg_mn`, teacher TP4, teacher FP8, teacher AWQ, **teacher size 14B / 8B** (the OPD-specific accuracy-vs-teacher-cost frontier), top_k ∈ {16, 32, 128} **re-validated @ lr3e-5** (the [OPD grid above](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218#issuecomment-4643446059) found these flat — but at lr1e-5 where nothing learned).

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
🤖
## Description
Follow-up to #6139 and related to #5328.

The current Grug ring EP path materializes global token/output buffers per rank. It all-gathers `x`, `selected_experts`, and `combine_weights`, gathers local expert assignments from `x_global`, then scatters into `out_global` before `psum_scatter` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:38`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:91`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py:110`). For small d2560/top-4 shapes this plumbing is a large fixed cost relative to expert math.

Add an assigned-token EP path that moves only routed assignments and produces the layout expected by `ragged_dot`: `x_dispatch`, assignment weights, return metadata, and local expert `group_sizes`. This can be a simpler single-node all-to-all/ragged path or a DeepEP handoff that avoids the extra local repack in `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` and `segment_sum` collapse (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py:50`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py:88`).

### Definition of Done
- No per-rank `x_global` or `out_global` activation buffer is required for the new path.
- Forward and backward match existing ring EP top-k combine semantics.
- Add a perf smoke test on the issue6044 d2560 shape comparing ring EP vs the new assigned-token path.
- Keep local GMM kernel work separate from this issue unless needed for the dispatch contract.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and related code
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PR; #6139 is the parent transport-gap issue)
- [x] Decide scope: too large for an auto-PR (new EP backend, fwd+bwd parity, perf smoke); posting analysis instead
- [ ] Human review of proposed approach before implementation

# Research

Ring EP forces every shard to materialize `x_global` and `out_global` of shape `(tokens * ep_size, D)` even though each shard only consumes its local-expert slice. At d2560/top-4 the all-gather + scatter + `psum_scatter` plumbing dominates expert math. The two existing alternatives both pay extra cost: `ragged_all_to_all` uses a slow transport primitive on B200 (#6139 numbers), and the DeepEP path does a host repack (`_pack_deepep_local_assignments`) plus a `segment_sum` collapse before/after the GMM that an assignment-native contract would skip.

**Relevant code**
- [`ep_ring.py#L38-L40`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L38-L40) — three full all-gathers per call
- [`ep_ring.py#L91-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L91-L93) — gather from `x_global`
- [`ep_ring.py#L110-L113`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py#L110-L113) — `out_global` scatter + `psum_scatter`
- [`ep_deepep.py#L43-L78`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py#L43-L78) — extra local repack producing `x_dispatch` shape
- [`ep_deepep.py#L81-L97`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py#L81-L97) — `segment_sum` collapse before combine transport

# Proposed Approach (design change, needs review)

Add a fourth EP backend `assigned_token` selected via the existing implementation knob at [`grug_moe.py#L208-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L208-L215). New file `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_assigned_token.py` exposes `_moe_mlp_ep_assigned_token_local(...)` with the same signature as the other three shard-local fns.

Dispatch contract: produce `(x_dispatch[TK_recv, D], assignment_weights[TK_recv], return_metadata, local_group_sizes[EL])` directly — the layout `ragged_dot` already consumes. No `x_global`, no `out_global`, no `segment_sum` collapse.

Sketch (shard-local, inside `shard_map("expert")`):

1. Per-shard expert-sorted permutation of routed assignments — reuse `_permute_by_global_expert` from `ep_common.py:44`. Each shard knows, for every global expert, how many of its own tokens land there.
2. Cross-shard sizing with one `all_gather` of the per-expert counts (small: `[num_experts]` int32, not `[tokens, D]` bf16). Derive `send_sizes` / `recv_sizes` for `ragged_all_to_all` of the routed-assignment payload — same shape calc as `ep_ragged_all_to_all.py:_shard_a2a_params` but built from per-edge counts so we never materialize `x_global`.
3. `ragged_all_to_all` of `(x_repeated_by_topk, combine_weight_repeated_by_topk)` into a receive buffer sized by `local_capacity = ceil(capacity_factor * assignments / ep_size)`. Capacity clipping reuses `_clip_receiver_group_sizes`.
4. Result is already grouped by local expert id → feed into `ragged_dot` directly (no `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` step).
5. Combine: multiply `out_dispatch` by `assignment_weights[:, None]` in place, then `ragged_all_to_all` with the transposed routing table back to the sender. On return, `_unpermute_from_global_expert` (already does the topk → token sum-combine) closes the loop.

Backward: the only custom-VJP-needing piece is the assignment permutation, which is already covered by `_sort_activations_custom` in `ep_common.py:17-31`. `ragged_all_to_all` has working autodiff on the existing path (`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`), so reuse that.

Differences vs. `ragged_all_to_all` backend: that one keeps a per-shard `x_global`-equivalent (`sorted_x` with `assignments_per_shard` rows, then compacts via `keep_mask`). The proposed path sends only the post-capacity tail and removes the round-trip `_compact_by_keep_mask` / `_expand_from_keep_mask` pair.

Differences vs. `deepep`: skip `_pack_deepep_local_assignments` (the receive buffer is already grouped) and skip `_collapse_deepep_local_assignments` (weights applied on the dispatch side).

# Validation Plan

- Unit test in `lib/levanter/tests/grug/` parameterized over `(EL, ep_size, topk, capacity_factor)` that runs both `_moe_mlp_ep_ring_local` and the new fn under a CPU `shard_map` with a 4-device fake mesh and checks `allclose` on forward output and on the W13/W2 gradients. This is the DoD "fwd/bwd match ring EP" gate.
- Drop-counter parity: confirm `dropped_total` matches ring under low capacity.
- Perf smoke on d2560/top-4 from #6044 — separate `@pytest.mark.slow` benchmark that records ring vs assigned-token wall-time and prints the ratio. Not asserted; the artifact is what's reviewed.

# Open Questions

1. Is `jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all` differentiable on B200/TPU in the configurations Grug ships, or is the existing `ep_ragged_all_to_all` path relying on a workaround? If a custom VJP is needed, this becomes a 300+ LOC change rather than 150.
2. Should this share a file with `ep_ragged_all_to_all.py` (both use `ragged_all_to_all`) or stay separate for the perf-comparison story #6139 asks for?
3. Capacity model: ring uses `local_capacity = ceil(capacity_factor * tokens * topk / ep_size)`. The assigned-token path can either match that or use a tighter per-expert cap. Match ring exactly for the parity test, leave tuning for follow-up?

Estimated size: ~150-250 LOC new code + ~100 LOC test = above the 100-line auto-PR threshold, hence asking for review first.

🤖
# Research

Ring EP still pays for per-rank global activation buffers in dispatch/combine, so it is the right comparator but not the scalable endpoint. A first assigned-token reference path using `jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all` avoids `x_global`/`out_global`, but a 4-GPU B200 d2560/top-4 forward smoke measured it much slower than ring, so plain XLA collectives are unlikely to satisfy this issue. The next viable path is CUDA-backed assignment transport or DeepEP dispatch with CUDA-side assignment packing/collapse, not more XLA repacking.

**Relevant code**
- [`ep_ring.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py) - global-buffer comparator
- [`ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py) - CUDA transport plus JAX repack/collapse
- [`transport_ffi.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/kernels/deepep/transport_ffi.py) - DeepEP JAX FFI/VJP surface

# Proposed Fix

Add an explicit `assigned_token` EP backend and benchmark harness as the reference contract: `x_dispatch`, assignment weights, return metadata, and local `group_sizes`. Then move the hot path to CUDA by extending the DeepEP FFI side with local assignment pack/collapse kernels so Grug does not do `top_k`/`take`/`segment_sum` around DeepEP receive buffers. Keep ring as the perf/correctness comparator until the CUDA path beats it on the d2560/top-4 smoke.

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This probe compared upstream-shaped FlashAttention-4 THD/varlen attention against Marin's current Grug segmented FA4/CuTe path on B200 for the exact d5120 Grug causal attention shape. The measured THD compact `cu_seqlens` path was materially faster than the current segmented FA4/CuTe implementation across the tested packed layouts, but the usable prototype is still a torch/DLPack bridge rather than a JIT-safe JAX FFI. The recommended integration direction is fixed max-segment metadata plus a real THD/JAX FFI path, while avoiding the private JAX cuDNN packed-offset path until its exact-GQA numerics are validated.

### Helpful links
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/issue5815-fa4-thd-logbook-20260529/.agents/logbooks/issue5815-fa4-thd.md
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6059
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Issue5815 needs a narrow benchmark of upstream-shaped FlashAttention-4 THD/varlen attention against the current Grug dense BSHD segmented FA4/CuTe port on B200. The target shape is the exact d5120 Grug causal self-attention q/k/v layout: q `[B,S,Hq,D]`, k/v `[B,S,Hkv,D]`.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether reshaping BSHD to THD, building `cu_seqlens` from packed segment IDs or fixed segment metadata, and calling upstream FA4 CuTe varlen materially beats the current segmented FA4 path for fwd+bwd. Thresholds: `<=0.005s` promising, `0.005-0.010s` marginal, `>0.010s` not worth pursuing for issue5815.

### Links

* Stable research tag: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/issue5815-fa4-thd-logbook-20260529
* Stable research logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/issue5815-fa4-thd-logbook-20260529/.agents/logbooks/issue5815-fa4-thd.md
* Stable probe script: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/issue5815-fa4-thd-logbook-20260529/scratch/issue5815_attention_backend_probe.py
* Draft PR: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6059
* Code paths: `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py`, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_thd.py`

## Results

Latest focused B200 probe for exact d5120, `S=4096,Hq=40,Hkv=8,D=128`, dynamic uneven segments:

| segs/row | B | dense upstream | current FA4/CuTe | THD fixed lengths | THD compact cu-lens |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1 | 0.000681s | 0.001939s | 0.000892s | 0.000656s |
| 2 | 4 | 0.002399s | 0.006653s | 0.002391s | 0.002151s |
| 4 | 1 | 0.000680s | 0.001280s | 0.000790s | 0.000561s |
| 4 | 4 | 0.002343s | 0.004249s | 0.002028s | 0.001801s |

## Decision log

* 2026-05-29: The public upstream PyTorch varlen wrapper alone was not enough; internal upstream FA4 `_flash_attn_fwd/_flash_attn_bwd` is the relevant API for the THD/cu-lens core.
* 2026-05-29: Fixed max-segment metadata is a useful integration point. It is materially faster than current segmented FA4/CuTe and avoids scanning full `[B,S]` segment IDs in the attention hot path.
* 2026-05-29: Do not use the private JAX cuDNN packed-offset path for exact Grug GQA until its GQA numerics are validated.

## Negative results index

* Public `flash_attn_varlen_func` autograd was slower than the internal upstream fwd/bwd API.
* Private JAX cuDNN packed offsets were fast but failed numerics for exact `Hq=40,Hkv=8` GQA.
* Including full dynamic `segment_ids -> cu_seqlens` construction inside the timed helper can erase the THD kernel win on small cases.

## Current baseline

Shape `B in {1,4} S=4096 Hq=40 Hkv=8 D=128`, bf16, causal fwd+bwd, dynamic uneven contiguous segments. Latest focused medians are listed in Results.
